Hey /u/kyprioth, I replied to your comment in this thread, but I wanted to reply to the parent post as well. I'm just one member of a team, so I don't want to put words in the other mods' mouths, but I understand where you're coming from and I agree that self-promotion can be excessive. What I would like to do is strike a good balance between allowing excessive self-promotion and outright banning well-meaning users from sharing their own gaming-related content with the community.

/v/gaming does have existing content creator guidelines that we have the ability to enforce, and cover excessive self-promotion as part of the existing community rules. If I notice (or someone reports) someone repeatedly posting their own content without participating in the community, I'll give them a head's up about it, and include some examples of how they can participate in the community (e.g. commenting on other people's posts, starting a discussion question, posting content that they're not affiliated with).

Some people like to comment, and some people just like to post, but there are ways for both kinds of contributors to involve themselves in the community instead of just using the sub for disposable content. If the same behavior continues, I can remove the posts, citing the community's content creator guidelines. Here is a good example from our modlog about what that removal process looks like, with included links to previous communications with that user.

Remember, /v/gaming's rules belong to its community, and reports help us enforce the rules you've helped us create. If you still feel that the rules as they exist aren't strong enough on self-promotion, we can have a discussion about it and try to improve them, but I hope that illustrating the rules as they exist has shown that we aren't without teeth on this issue already.
